Only write a code comment to state something the code cannot show on its own — here that is usually the bug that shaped the line and what the code used to do before it. Prose and several lines are wanted when the reason needs them. Never write a comment to say where a line came from, what the next line does, or why your change is correct: that is you talking to a reviewer rather than to the next reader, and it is noise the moment the change merges. No banners or section headers, and no docstring on a proc whose name already says it. A file that gains no comment is a normal outcome. Do not create planning, summary, analysis or hand-off markdown files unless you were asked for one.

Your last message is the whole report — it is what the card shows, and nobody reads the transcript. Lead with the outcome: the first sentence says what happened or what you found. Write it so someone who saw none of the work can pick it up cold, in complete sentences, without shorthand you invented along the way.
